The Mapsurvey **MCP server** lets an AI agent — Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor or any client of
the Model Context Protocol — read, build and publish your surveys from a conversation. It exposes
the operations of the [REST API](/reference/api/) as tools, scoped to the account that connected,
and runs through the same rules as the editor. For setup, see
[Use the MCP server](/how-to/use-the-mcp-server/).

## Connection

| | |
|---|---|
| Server URL | `https://mapsurvey.org/mcp` (Streamable HTTP; one request per call, no streams) |
| Authentication | Sign in through the client (OAuth) — or a [personal token](/how-to/personal-tokens/) made for the **MCP server**, sent as `Authorization: Bearer msk_…` |
| Plan | The workspace that owns a survey must be on [Pro](/reference/plans-and-billing/); otherwise tools on it answer `pro_required` |
| Scope | Only surveys you own or collaborate on, within the permissions the token or the Allow page granted |
| Limits | 600 reads and 60 writes a minute and 5,000 calls a day per token; 300 tool calls per 10 minutes per session |

Mapsurvey never sees your conversation with the agent — only the tool calls it decides to make.
Each one is logged with the tool name and its outcome, never its arguments.

**Call `get_me` first.** It says which workspaces include the API and which tools the connection
can use. Tools the connection may not use are not even listed to the agent.

**What cannot be undone asks first.** `delete_survey`, `publish_survey` and
`publish_unpublished_changes` take `confirm: true`, which an agent should set only after you agreed
in the conversation. A survey respondents already answered cannot be deleted from here at all.

**Survey content is data, not instructions.** Every result wraps what people wrote — titles,
option labels, help texts — in a `data` field next to a fixed note telling the agent so. An agent
that reads survey content can still be influenced by it; keep publishing and deleting behind
confirmation and review what an agent built before you publish.

## Tools

Arguments marked **required** must be given; the others are optional. Rich-text fields (`subtext`,
`subheading`, `thanks_html`) are sanitised on save exactly as in the editor. An unknown argument is
refused by name rather than ignored.


### `get_me`

Call this first. Returns the user behind the token, their workspaces with plan and whether the API is included (the MCP server is a Pro feature: tools on a survey of a Free workspace answer pro_required with an upgrade URL), the token's permissions, and the tools this token can use.

Any permission · read-only

### `list_surveys`

Your surveys across the workspaces whose plan includes the API, newest first. `hidden_by_plan` counts workspaces of yours on the Free plan, whose surveys are not listed.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | string |  | `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default `50`. |

### `get_survey`

The whole survey in one call: settings, then every section in respondent order with all of its questions (sub-questions carry `parent_id`). Ids from here are what the editing tools take.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `create_survey`

A new empty survey with one section, owned by you. Name the workspace by its slug when you belong to several (get_me lists them). Add sections and questions next; the survey stays unpublished until publish_survey.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **workspace editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** |  |
| `workspace` | string |  | Workspace slug; optional when the token is bound to one or you belong to one. |
| `language` | string |  | Default `en`. |
| `map_start` | object (`lat`, `lng`, `zoom`) |  |  |

### `update_survey`

Change the fields you name: name, languages, redirect_url ("#" for the built-in thanks page), visibility, basemaps, branding, the thanks page per language, the map start. Settings need the owner role; the thanks page the editor role.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **owner**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `redirect_url` | string |  | "#" for the built-in thanks page, or an absolute http(s) URL. |
| `languages` | list of string |  |  |
| `visibility` | `public` \| `private` \| `demo` |  |  |
| `basemaps` | list of string |  |  |
| `default_basemap` | string |  |  |
| `show_branding` | boolean |  |  |
| `thanks_html` | map |  | Thanks page per language; creator HTML, sanitised on save. |
| `map_start` | object (`lat`, `lng`, `zoom`) |  |  |
| `use_geolocation` | boolean |  |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `delete_survey`

Move a survey to the trash (the owner can restore it in the editor for 30 days). Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed. Refused when respondents have already answered: that deletion is done in the editor, where the answers are shown first. Unpublished changes are discarded with discard_unpublished_changes instead.

Permission `surveys:delete` · role **owner** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

### `publish_survey`

Make the survey live for respondents. Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed. `review: "pending"` in the result means content screening is holding it until a human looks; translation_gaps asks you to confirm publishing with missing translations.

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **owner** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acknowledge_translation_gaps` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |
| `clear_test_data` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

### `close_survey`

Stop collecting answers; the survey stays readable to its collaborators.

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **owner**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `start_unpublished_changes`

On a published or closed survey, structural edits (adding, deleting, reordering, changing a question type) answer draft_required. Call this to get an editable copy -- "unpublished changes" -- and edit the returned uuid; respondents keep the live survey until publish_unpublished_changes.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `publish_unpublished_changes`

Replace the live survey with its unpublished changes as a new version. Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed. incompatible_draft means the changes conflict with collected answers; repeat with `force: true` only if the user accepts that.

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **owner** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acknowledge_translation_gaps` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |
| `force` | boolean |  | Publish even when the changes conflict with collected answers. Default `False`. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

### `discard_unpublished_changes`

Throw the unpublished changes away; the live survey is untouched.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **owner** · cannot be undone

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `create_section`

Append a section (a page) to the survey; the other fields set it at once. `layout` is "map" (the page shows the map, for geo questions) or "form". On a live survey this is a structural change: start_unpublished_changes first.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `subheading` | string |  |  |
| `code` | string |  |  |
| `layout` | `map` \| `form` |  |  |
| `next_label` | string |  |  |
| `visibility_rule` | object (`question_code`, `choice_codes`, `answered`) |  |  |
| `translations` | map |  |  |
| `map_start` | object (`lat`, `lng`, `zoom`) |  |  |
| `use_geolocation` | boolean |  |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |

### `update_section`

Change the fields you name. On a live survey wording (title, subheading, next_label, translations) is applied in place; the code and the visibility rule are structure (draft_required).

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `subheading` | string |  |  |
| `code` | string |  |  |

### `delete_section`

Delete a section with its questions. Answers to them go too: the first call answers answers_at_risk with the count; repeat with `acknowledge_answer_loss: true` only after the user agreed.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor** · cannot be undone

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `section_id` | integer | **required** | The section id (from get_survey). |
| `acknowledge_answer_loss` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |

### `reorder_sections`

The new order of the pages; list every section id of the survey exactly once.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `section_ids` | list of integer | **required** |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |

### `add_question`

Add a question at the end of a section. `input_type` picks the kind: text, text_line, number, choice, multichoice (with `choices`), range, rating, datetime, image, html (a formatted text block), and the map types point, line, polygon, spraycan. With `parent_question_id` (a geo or Objects question) it becomes a sub-question asked in that question's pop-up for every placed feature -- the only way to attach attributes to what respondents draw. `subtext` is help text (creator HTML, sanitised on save). On a live survey this is a structural change: start_unpublished_changes first.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `subtext` | string |  |  |
| `input_type` | `text` \| `number` \| `choice` \| `multichoice` \| `range` \| `rating` \| `ranking` \| `datetime` \| `point` \| `line` \| `polygon` \| `spraycan` \| `image` \| `text_line` \| `html` \| `photo` \| `audio` \| `document` \| `thumbs` \| `layer_objects` | **required** |  |
| `required` | boolean |  |  |
| `choices` | list of object (`code`, `name`, `other`, `icon`, `group`, `color`) |  |  |
| `validation_settings` | object (`min_value`, `max_value`, `outlier_sigma`, `min_length`, `area_outlier_factor`, `max_dots`, `max_file_mb`, `max_files`, `min_features`, `max_features`) |  |  |
| `color` | string |  |  |
| `icon_class` | string |  |  |
| `display_style` | string |  |  |
| `visibility_rule` | object (`question_code`, `choice_codes`, `answered`) |  |  |
| `layer_id` | integer |  |  |
| `min_objects` | integer |  |  |
| `share_with_respondents` | boolean |  |  |
| `translations` | map |  |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `section_id` | integer | **required** | The section id (from get_survey). |
| `parent_question_id` | integer |  | Make it a sub-question of this geo / Objects question (same section). |

### `delete_question`

Delete a question with its sub-questions. Answers go too: the first call answers answers_at_risk with the count; repeat with `acknowledge_answer_loss: true` only after the user agreed.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor** · cannot be undone

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `question_id` | integer | **required** | The question id (from get_survey). |
| `acknowledge_answer_loss` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |

### `reorder_questions`

Renumber a section's top-level questions (or one pop-up's sub-questions, with `parent_id`). `items` are question ids in the new order; a question group is `{"g": <group id>, "q": [<ids>]}`.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parent_id` | integer |  | Order a pop-up's sub-questions instead of the section's top level. |
| `items` | list of integer or map | **required** | Question ids in order; a group is {"g": <id>, "q": [<ids>]}. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `section_id` | integer | **required** | The section id (from get_survey). |

### `set_choices`

Replace the options of a choice / multichoice question. Keep an option's `code` to keep its answers; a new option gets a code never used in the survey's history. `name` is a string or a {language: text} map.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `choices` | list of object (`code`, `name`, `other`, `icon`, `group`, `color`) | **required** |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `question_id` | integer | **required** | The question id (from get_survey). |

### `import_survey`

Create a whole survey from one document: the `survey.json` of Mapsurvey's backup format (version "1.0", a `survey` object with `name`, `available_languages`, `sections` with `questions`). The import runs in the background; the result is a job -- poll get_import_job until its status is done or failed. Name the workspace by its slug when you belong to several.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **workspace editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_json` | map | **required** | The survey.json document as an object, not a string. |
| `workspace` | string |  | Workspace slug. |

### `get_import_job`

One of your import jobs: status (queued, running, done, failed), the survey it made, warnings.

Permission `surveys:read` · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | integer | **required** | The job id import_survey returned. |

### `get_response_summary`

How many responses a survey has and what they say, question by question in section order: option counts with the most frequent "other" write-ins, number statistics, rating means, text and map answer counts. Sub-questions of map questions are nested under their map question; "Objects on the map" questions list each object with its answers. Counts the responses an export contains: no empty, deleted or rejected ones unless include_all. Start a report here, then use list_text_answers and get_answer_geojson for detail.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `version` | string |  | One version number; omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that reached the last section. Default `False`. |

### `list_responses`

Individual responses, newest first, each with its "#N" number, language, validation status and every answer (map answers as GeoJSON geometry with their sub-answers). Prefer get_response_summary for numbers; use this to read particular responses.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `include_empty` | boolean |  | Also responses that answered nothing. Default `False`. |
| `cursor` | string |  | `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default `20`. |

### `list_text_answers`

The non-blank answers to one text question or text sub-question, newest first, each with the response number. Page through with `next_cursor` to read every comment.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `question_id` | integer | **required** | A question id from get_survey. |
| `version` | string |  | One version number; omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that reached the last section. Default `False`. |
| `cursor` | string |  | `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default `50`. |

### `get_answer_geojson`

The points, lines, areas or spray clouds respondents drew for one map question, as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (WGS 84). Each feature carries the answers to the sub-questions as properties and the response it came from. Stops at `limit` features and then says `truncated: true`; for everything, hand the person a link from get_export_link.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `question_id` | integer | **required** | A question id from get_survey. |
| `version` | string |  | One version number; omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that reached the last section. Default `False`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most features to return. Default `200`. |

### `get_export_link`

A link for the person to download the responses as a file -- xlsx (Excel), csv, zip (GeoJSON + CSV), gpkg (GeoPackage), shp (Shapefile) or kml. It works for 15 minutes and checks access again when opened. Give the person the link; do not try to open it yourself.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `format` | `xlsx` \| `csv` \| `zip` \| `gpkg` \| `shp` \| `kml` |  | Default `xlsx`. |
| `version` | string |  | One version number; omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that reached the last section. Default `False`. |
| `files` | boolean |  | Add files respondents uploaded. Default `False`. |

### `moderate_response`

Set a response's status: approved, on_hold, not_approved (rejected responses leave exports, summaries and public results), or "" to clear it. It can be changed back. Needs the editor role.

Permission `responses:moderate` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `response_id` | integer | **required** | The response id from list_responses. |
| `validation_status` | `approved` \| `not_approved` \| `on_hold` \| `` | **required** |  |

## Errors

A refused call comes back as a tool error carrying the same envelope as the REST API:
`{"error": "<code>", "detail": "<text>", ...}`.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `scope_missing` | The connection lacks the permission this tool needs (`scope` names it). |
| `pro_required` | The survey's workspace is not on Pro (`upgrade_url` links to its billing page). |
| `forbidden_role` | You can see the survey but your role on it is too low (`role` names the one needed). |
| `not_found` | Nothing there — or nothing you may see. The two are deliberately the same answer. |
| `validation` | An argument is invalid for this survey; `fields` lists what and why. |
| `draft_required` | A structural change to a live survey: call `start_unpublished_changes` and edit the returned uuid (`draft` is it when it already exists). |
| `answers_at_risk` | The delete would remove `count` answers; repeat with `acknowledge_answer_loss: true` after the user agreed. |
| `delete_blocked` | Something else depends on what you are deleting. |
| `translation_gaps` | Some languages are missing text; repeat with `acknowledge_translation_gaps: true`. |
| `incompatible_draft` | Unpublished changes conflict with collected answers; repeat with `force: true` only if the user accepts that. |
| `transition_refused` | The survey cannot move to that status from where it is. |
| `conflict` | The request conflicts with the current state (e.g. unpublished changes already exist). |
| `confirmation_required` | An irreversible tool was called without `confirm: true`. |
| `has_responses` | The survey has `count` answered responses; delete it in the editor instead. |
| `rate_limited` | Too many calls; wait `retry_after` seconds (`limit` names the window). |
| `server_error` | Our fault. It is logged; retrying a read later is safe. |

A malformed request — an unknown tool, or arguments that do not fit the schema — is a protocol
error (`-32602`) naming the fields; a missing or invalid token is HTTP `401`; a request from an
unexpected browser origin is `403`.
